startup.name: Travo
startup.description: Travo has no description in the input (one liner and description are a single period). It is tagged Real Estate and Construction with a team of 4 in San Francisco in the Winter 2026 batch, and its site name suggests an AI product. I assume it sells AI software to construction or real estate firms, paid per seat or per project.

yc_acceptance.basis: Already in the Winter 2026 batch, so reported for completeness. Start at the roughly 1 percent prior, with a small lift for a four person team and AI for construction fitting YC interest, and no information on traction or founders, so I stay near the prior with a wide band.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because AI for construction and real estate workflow already had YC companies (PermitFlow W22, InspectMind W24, PermitPortal F24), and with no description the application cannot show a distinct wedge, customer or traction, so reviewers would have to guess the problem, the buyer and why this team is the right one.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry 'Real Estate and Construction': seed 42% / 53% / 62%, cond 53% (n=36). Timing: time_to_milestones.csv industry:Real Estate and Construction months_to_seed p25 2.2, p50 6, p75 18.75.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor of 0.53 is the ever reached figure, from only 36 companies so wide. The window is 10 months from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17; this cohort has a median of 6 months and p75 of 18.75, so about 55 to 60 percent of eventual raisers are inside it, about 0.30. I lower slightly to 0.28 because the input is empty, with no product evidence at all. The odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round of $1M to $3M, typical when a two to four person team raises from angels and micro funds soon after demo day. Construction AI seeds in the records ran from $5.5M for PermitFlow to small rounds, and with no information I keep the default shape tilted low.

Institutional seed of $3M to $6M, near the 2022 and later median of $3.5M in round_benchmarks.csv, which includes the YC deal so it reads low. Construction AI seeds in the records ran from $5.5M for PermitFlow to small rounds, and with no information I keep the default shape tilted low.
Larger institutional seed of $6M to $12M, where press covered 2026 raises had their median of $6.0M; needs live revenue or a standout founder story.
Upside seed above $12M, seen in 2025 voice, document and agent categories when a lab style team is bid up by several funds.

ladder.why_it_fails: The most likely miss is that a four person company with no public product statement has nothing for seed investors to underwrite beyond the YC deal, in a crowded field where PermitFlow, InspectMind and PermitPortal already have AI construction products. Several construction startups in the records raised only YC money, so a small angel check below $1M is the likely path.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry 'Real Estate and Construction': series_a cond 47% (n=19), ever 25% known-only, range 20% to 40%; tiny sample.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is the ever reached figure. The forecast window is 10 months from the as of date, and months_to_series_a in time_to_milestones.csv has a median near 28 to 35 months, so only a small share of eventual Series A raisers get there inside the window. Hence the probability is well below the anchor.

bands.rationale: Thin or small Series A, common for vertical software with early but modest revenue.
Central band around the 2022 and later Series A median of $15M with p25 $11M.
Strong growth round led by a top tier fund.
Upside where the category is hot and revenue compounds fast.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A requires clear revenue from contractors or developers, who adopt software slowly, and a niche where larger AI players such as PermitFlow do not dominate. With a seed arriving late in the window, an A inside it is unlikely. PermitFlow needed about nine months from seed to its Series A, which is the benchmark leader pace.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry 'Real Estate and Construction': series_b cond 22% (n=9), ever 6% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Series B inside a window of 10 months is rare: months_to_series_b has a median of 36 to 47 months from the batch start in time_to_milestones.csv, so almost no company reaches it this fast. Only a breakout would.

bands.rationale: Thin Series B or extension round, used when growth slowed after the Series A and investors price the company on revenue multiples alone.
Central band; 2022 and later Series B median is $40M.
Hot company band; 2022 and later post money median is $600M.
Breakout upside where one lead investor competes hard for a category leader with fast revenue growth and strong net retention.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B inside 10 months is a tail event. Only a standout like PermitFlow reached a Series B, and it took nearly four years from its start in 2022 to December 2025. Construction adoption cycles are long, so the realistic outcome inside the window is that no Series B happens, and even a good seed would leave the company short of the revenue lenders and growth funds expect.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry 'Real Estate and Construction': series_c cond 0% (n=2), ever 0% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is conditional on Series B, ever reached. Inside the window almost nobody gets to Series C, and I keep the figure low and nonzero for a breakout path with several quick rounds.

bands.rationale: Thin extension or flat round, used when growth slowed after the Series B and investors price the company on revenue multiples alone.
Central band; 2022 and later Series C median is $74M.
Strong growth round led by a large crossover or growth fund after the company shows durable revenue and net retention above 110 percent.
Category leader upside where the company is among the top two in its market and raises at a premium multiple to scale internationally.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C inside the window is almost impossible: the cohort has none and the sector's best company needed years to reach a B. Only an extraordinary scale up with several rounds in a few months would produce it, and nothing in the input suggests that.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Likely outcomes are a stall or small sale as construction and real estate customers adopt slowly and incumbents bundle AI. Laguna (W20) and Spaces Life (W09) are inactive with almost no footprint, Sakneen stopped at a $1.1M seed, and Ladder was acquired with little capital, so most companies in this sector end small.

narrative.headline: A blank application in a funded but slow-adopting sector; a priced seed inside 10 months is under one in three.
narrative.general_summary: Travo has no description in the input, only a Real Estate and Construction tag and a team of four. The sector has a strong funding story for AI, with PermitFlow as the breakout, but also many small or inactive companies and slow customer adoption. With no product information I stay near the cohort timing for seed and reduce slightly for the empty description. For the 10 month window the seed probability is about 0.28, a Series A inside the window is unlikely, and if it raises the most likely size is $1M to $3M. The odds do not rank Travo against other companies and rest on very thin evidence.

assumptions: Only the input file was used; the one liner and description are just a period, so the product is assumed from the tag and site name.
Seed means a round above about $1M from outside investors, not the standard YC deal.
Search results dated after 2026-01-05 were treated as market context for other companies only.
